title: Decided Upstream, Written Late: Locating and Pricing the Cross-Lingual Refusal Circuit of a Multilingual MoE
abstract: arXiv:2608.08032v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Safety alignment in multilingual models is uneven: a model that reliably refuses a harmful request in English will often comply with the same request in a lower-resource language. We trace this gap mechanistically in sarvam, an Indic-multilingual mixture-of-experts reasoning model, and find it is not a failure to detect harm. Harm is encoded as an internal direction that is nearly language-invariant in mid-network (English-vs-Indic cosine ${\approx}0.9$ at $L11$), and steering that direction upstream causally controls refusal. But the detection direction is orthogonal to the change that actually writes the refusal, which is late and assembled over the course of generation rather than read off in a single forward pass. translated_title: 上游决策，下游书写：定位与定价多语言MoE中的跨语言拒绝回路
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.08032v2 公告类型：替换 摘要：多语言模型的安全对齐是不均匀的：一个在英语中可靠拒绝有害请求的模型，在低资源语言中往往会对相同请求妥协。我们在sarvam（一个印度语多语言专家混合推理模型）中从机制上追踪了这一差距，并发现这并非检测危害的失败。危害被编码为一个内部方向，该方向在网络中层几乎与语言无关（英语与印度语余弦相似度在L11层约0.9），且在上游引导该方向可因果控制拒绝行为。但检测方向与真正书写拒绝的更改正交，后者发生得较晚，并在生成过程中逐步组装，而非在单次前向传播中直接读出。我们将书写归因于一个特定的、可定位的回路，一个由注意力对抗者制约的专家混合书写器，并定价了对其干预的每种方式：抑制对抗者既便宜又有效，而放大……
tldr: 该论文揭示多语言MoE模型的安全拒绝失败源于一个可定位的“书写”回路，该回路与语言无关的危害检测方向正交，且通过抑制注意力对抗者可以低成本高效地恢复拒绝行为。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals that safety refusal failures in multilingual MoE models stem from a localizable "writing" circuit orthogonal to language-invariant harm detection, where damping the attention opposer offers a cheap and effective intervention.
